Samuel H. Miller built a Cleveland career that joined business leadership at Forest City Enterprises with wide service to the city’s civic, educational, medical, and religious institutions.

A graduate of Case Western Reserve University with an MBA from Harvard Business School, Miller served in the U.S. Navy from 1942 to 1946. He became a key stakeholder in Forest City in 1947 and went on to oversee various areas of the company. He is particularly credited with spearheading Forest City’s move into land development.

Miller became the company’s treasurer in 1992 and was named chairman of the board in 1993. In 1995, Albert B. Ratner joined him as co-chairman of the board, and Miller became co-chairman emeritus of Forest City Enterprises.

Beyond Forest City, Miller was actively engaged in the Cleveland community and became a nationally recognized leader in the Jewish community. He was named a Lifetime Honorary Trustee of the Jewish Community Federation of Cleveland and of the National Conference of Christians and Jews, and he served on the board of trustees of the Jewish National Fund.

His board service reached across the city’s institutions. Miller served as a trustee of the Urban League, WVIZ, Crime Stoppers, the Police Memorial, Medical Mutual of Ohio, and the Catholic Diocese of Cleveland Foundation. In education, he served on the boards of Cleveland State University, Baldwin-Wallace College, Notre Dame College, and John Carroll University, and was named an Honorary Trustee of Case Western Reserve University. He also took part in the Greater Cleveland Roundtable.

Miller served on the board of directors and executive committee of The Cleveland Clinic, and in 2003 he was made a Distinguished Fellow of The Cleveland Clinic Foundation.

In 2013, he was inducted into the Cleveland International Hall of Fame.

Miller’s Cleveland legacy lies in that breadth: a business leader who helped guide Forest City, and a trustee whose service reached Jewish, Catholic, civic, educational, and medical institutions alike.
